sources.citation: Wichmann, Soeren. 1994. Mixe-Zoquean linguistics: a status report. In: Bartholomew, Lastra & Manrique (eds.), Panorama de los estudios de las lenguas indigenas de Mexico, vol. 1, pp. 193-267. Quito: Abya-Yala.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Discusses stress only for living languages (e.g. Chiapas Zoque South stress shift). For Tapachultec the only phonological remark is 'Tapachultec has a lowering of */a/ to /e/' (p. 229); notes it became extinct in the first half of the 20th c. and reviews its classification (Lehmann 1915/1920, Wonderly 1949, Kaufman 1964a 'Chiapas Mixe'). Silent on Tapachultec stress.

sources.citation: Kaufman, Terrence. 1965. [Report on research submitted to the Chair of Linguistics, UC Berkeley, 7 Oct 1965].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: '"Reconstitution" of Tapachultec (March-April 1965). Tapachultec is quite possibly extinct, and is attested in only 5 short and not very accurate word lists.. philological methods.. allow one to salvage and interpret most of the extant material.' Nothing on stress; shows Kaufman's unpublished reconstitution exists.

sources.citation: Lehmann, Walter. 1915. Ueber die Stellung und Verwandtschaft der Subtiaba-Sprache der pazifischen Kueste Nicaraguas und ueber die Sprache von Tapachula in Suedchiapas. Zeitschrift fuer Ethnologie 47: 1-34.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. This is the primary publication of both extant Tapachultec vocabularies (A. Johnston 1888; Sapper-Ricke 1911) in parallel columns with Mixe/Zoque comparanda (pp. 26-34) plus a classificatory discussion (p. 25). No remark on Betonung/accent. The Spanish-orthography transcriptions do carry acute accents, overwhelmingly on the final syllable (i-apé 'father', i-mén 'child', min-apó, min-acá, gojpié 'head', min-ix-cú/tan-ix-cú 'eye', bats-cú 'arm', tan-techequé 'ear', min-géu 'mouth', chizí/xixé 'meat', ut-mechú/metsú 'night', an-xú 'I go', mi-xú; one initial: cópi 'hurry!') -- raw data o…
